title: What expression do these steps give?
description: Two numbers are added, and the sum is multiplied by half of the sum. The steps are written as an expression with letters and shown to equal half of the square of the sum, then checked with the numbers three and five.
teaching_notes: One idea: a rule that works for any two numbers is written once with letters, and the sum times itself is the square of the sum. Watch for students who halve each number before adding.

source: Figure it Out (identities and patterns, question 8)
video_script.why: The child has shown that expressions for one region are equal by working with them, and now shows that a rule given in words equals a short expression.
video_script.substitution: Write the sum with letters, write half of the sum, multiply them, and check the result with the numbers three and five.
video_script.anchor: two number cards a and b, with the steps add, then multiply by half of the sum
video_script.payoff_line: The result is half of the square of the sum

final_answer.spoken: the sum times half of the sum is half of the square of the sum

never_show: a/2 + b as the half of the sum
maths_rules: the two numbers are a and b; their sum is a + b
half of the sum is (a + b)/2
the result is (a + b) × (a + b)/2 = (a + b)²/2 = (1/2)(a + b)²
(a + b) × (a + b) = (a + b)², the square of the sum
check with 3 and 5: sum 8, half of the sum 4, 8 × 4 = 32; square of the sum 64, half of 64 is 32
video_script.design: One idea: write the steps once with letters, then see the sum times itself as a square. The two number cards stay in the anchor band; the working board holds each line.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='cards'/>Take any two numbers, and add them together.
<bookmark mark='steps'/>Then multiply this by half of the sum of the two numbers.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write an expression for these steps. Then prove the result is half of the square of the sum.

<bookmark mark='work'/>Working with the expressions showed that they were equal, as it did for the slanting region.

beats.on_screen: Given: any two numbers a and b; add them, then multiply by half of the sum

marks.given: the given steps are written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, any two numbers eigh and b. We add them, then multiply by half of the sum.

beats.on_screen: To find: an expression for the steps. To prove: it is half of the square of the sum

marks.find: the two things to do are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write the expression, and show it is half of the square of the sum.

beats.on_screen: sum of the two numbers = a + b

marks.sum: the sum a + b is written

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>First, add the two numbers, and their sum is eigh plus b.

beats.on_screen: half of the sum = (a + b)/2; the steps give (a + b) × (a + b)/2

marks.half: half of the sum, (a + b)/2, is written

narration: <bookmark mark='half'/>Second, take half of the sum, which is eigh plus b, divided by two.
<bookmark mark='mul'/>Multiply the sum by it. The expression is eigh plus b, times, eigh plus b over two.

marks.half: (a + b)²/2 is written with the words half of the square of the sum

beats.colours: the square of the sum in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='square'/>Third, the sum times the sum is the square of the sum, eigh plus b all squared.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Divide by two to get eigh plus b all squared, over two. That is half of the square of the sum.

beats.on_screen: put the answer back: a = 3, b = 5: sum 8, half of the sum 4, 8 × 4 = 32; square of the sum 64, half of 64 = 32

marks.back: the words put the answer back in the question are written with a = 3 and b = 5
marks.steps: sum 8, half of the sum 4 and 8 × 4 = 32 are written
marks.half: the square of the sum 64 and half of 64 = 32 are written and ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Fourth, put the answer back in the question, and take three and five.
<bookmark mark='steps'/>Their sum is eight, and half of it is four. Eight times four is thirty two.
<bookmark mark='half'/>The square of the sum is sixty four, and half of it is thirty two, so both agree.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The steps give the sum times half of the sum. The result is half of the square of the sum.
